source.text: Points (a), (b) and (c) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 1 and the second subparagraph thereof shall not apply

items.label: Derogation: important reasons of public interest

items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, the transfer is necessary for important public-interest reasons recognised by the applicable Union or Member State law.

items.label: Derogation: legal claims

items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, this transfer is necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

items.label: Derogation: vital interests

sources.text: the transfer is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of other persons, where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent

items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, this transfer is necessary to protect vital interests of the data subject or other persons and the data subject is physically or legally incapable of consent.

items.label: Derogation: public register

sources.text: the transfer is made from a register which according to Union or Member State law is intended to provide information to the public

items.statement: Without adequacy or safeguards, the transfer is from a register intended by law to inform the public and open to consultation under applicable conditions; those conditions hold, the whole register or entire categories are not transferred, and any legitimate-interest access restriction is respected (Art. 49(1)(g), (2)).

items.label: Derogation: compelling legitimate interests (last resort)

sources.text: may take place only if the transfer is not repetitive, concerns only a limited number of data subjects

source.text: Points (a), (b) and (c) of the first subparagraph of paragraph 1 and the second subparagraph thereof shall not apply

items.statement: Neither Art. 45 nor 46 nor any first-subparagraph Art. 49(1) derogation can support the transfer. It is not repetitive, concerns only a limited number of data subjects, is necessary for compelling controller interests not overridden by data-subject interests or rights, and the controller has assessed all circumstances, supplied suitable safeguards, informed the supervisory authority and data subjects, and documented the assessment and safeguards under Art. 49(6).

statement.before: Irish law permits research processing of special categories subject to the Health Research Regulations' mandatory suitable and specific measures, including explicit consent unless an exception or Committee declaration applies.
statement.after: For personal data processed for health research, the Health Research Regulations impose suitable and specific measures, including the current consent/declaration/exception conditions. These are additional measures and do not themselves supply a GDPR Art. 6 basis or replace an Art. 9(2) condition.

note.after: Selected consent alternatives are represented. Transitional, capacity and special sector legislation require case-specific review; the graph does not claim this is an exhaustive list.

statement.before: Irish law supplies the basis for public-task processing: processing is lawful to the extent necessary and proportionate for a function conferred by or under an enactment or the Constitution.
statement.after: DPA 2018 s. 38(1) supports processing necessary and proportionate for a statutory or constitutional function, including administering a non-statutory scheme, programme or funds whose administration has that legal basis. It does not itself identify this controller’s particular function.

statement.before: Irish law permits processing of special categories for public interest reasons in the area of public health, with suitable and specific measures.
statement.after: Irish law permits processing of special categories for public interest reasons in the area of public health, with suitable and specific measures. The processing must be necessary for the public-health interest identified in s. 53.
